question: Why should an OIT record an abnormal process condition and the response taken at the time it occurs?
optionA: To preserve an accurate operational history for control, communication and compliance follow-up
optionB: To replace all laboratory results with the operator's visual assessment of the process
optionC: To allow later shifts to change the original reading when conditions return to normal
optionD: To avoid notifying the operator in charge until the monthly report has been prepared
options: To preserve an accurate operational history for control, communication and compliance follow-up
To replace all laboratory results with the operator's visual assessment of the process
To allow later shifts to change the original reading when conditions return to normal
To avoid notifying the operator in charge until the monthly report has been prepared
correctAnswer: To preserve an accurate operational history for control, communication and compliance follow-up
explanation: Contemporaneous records support safe process control, shift communication, troubleshooting and regulatory accountability. Entries should be factual and should not be rewritten to hide abnormal conditions.
sourceTitle: Ontario Regulation 129/04 - Licensing of Sewage Works Operators

question: Effluent quality is deteriorating rapidly and the cause is not yet confirmed. What is the best OIT response?
optionA: Delay reporting until laboratory confirmation identifies a single definitive cause
optionB: Change several process set points at once so at least one adjustment improves the effluent
optionC: Notify the responsible operator, preserve accurate data and begin the approved upset-response procedure
optionD: Record only the final stable readings so the operating log does not contain conflicting data
options: Delay reporting until laboratory confirmation identifies a single definitive cause
Change several process set points at once so at least one adjustment improves the effluent
Notify the responsible operator, preserve accurate data and begin the approved upset-response procedure
Record only the final stable readings so the operating log does not contain conflicting data
correctAnswer: Notify the responsible operator, preserve accurate data and begin the approved upset-response procedure
explanation: A rapidly developing upset requires prompt escalation, accurate records and controlled response. Simultaneous untracked changes can hide the cause and worsen the condition.

question: A blocked sewer must be accessed through a manhole in an active traffic lane. What must occur before the cover is removed?
optionA: Park the service truck directly over the manhole and rely on its hazard lights alone
optionB: Establish the approved traffic-control zone and protect workers, road users and the open access
optionC: Remove the cover first so the blockage can be assessed before traffic-control equipment is placed
optionD: Ask the attendant to stand in the lane and wave vehicles around the unprotected work area
options: Park the service truck directly over the manhole and rely on its hazard lights alone
Establish the approved traffic-control zone and protect workers, road users and the open access

correctAnswer: Establish the approved traffic-control zone and protect workers, road users and the open access
